title: Particle Physics
subject: Particles & Fields
summary: A survey of the Standard Model following Griffiths: particle zoo and history, relativistic kinematics, symmetries, bound states, the Feynman calculus, QED, QCD, weak interactions and neutrinos, and gauge theories with the Higgs mechanism.

units.title: The Particle Landscape
units.summary: How the electron, photon, antimatter, neutrinos, strange particles and quarks were discovered, what the Standard Model contains, and how forces become Feynman diagrams.

lessons.title: Early Discoveries and the Neutrino Puzzle in Beta Decay
objectives: Order the key discoveries (electron, nucleus, photon, positron, neutron, muon, pion, neutrino) and state which puzzle each one solved or created
Explain why beta-decay energy spectra forced Pauli's neutrino hypothesis

lectures.title: Introduction to Nuclear and Particle Physics: full video-lecture series (11 chapters)
Lecture 0.5: Early History and People in Nuclear and Particle Physics

demoIdeas: Timeline explorer: scroll through 1897-1983 and see the particle table fill in as each discovery lands, with the puzzle each one solved or created.
Beta-decay spectrum: toggle between a two-body decay (a line at fixed electron energy) and a three-body decay with a neutrino (continuous spectrum with endpoint) and see the energy sharing.

lessons.title: Yukawa's Pion, Dirac's Positron and the Particle Families
objectives: Explain Dirac's prediction of the positron and Yukawa's prediction of the pion from the range of the nuclear force
Distinguish leptons, hadrons, mesons and baryons by their interactions
demoIdeas: Yukawa range calculator: slider for mediator mass shows the range hbar/mc and the potential e^{-r/R}/r against the Coulomb 1/r.
Pair creation and annihilation: toggle gamma -> e+ e- near a nucleus and e+ e- -> gamma gamma, tracking charge and energy conservation.

lessons.title: Strangeness and the Quark Model of Hadrons
objectives: State what strangeness is and why strange particles are produced in pairs but decay slowly
Build the lowest meson and baryon multiplets from quark content and state the quark charges needed to get integer hadron charges

lectures.title: Lecture 1.1: Quantum Field and Matter (strangeness and the quark model)

demoIdeas: Quark-content builder: drag u, d, s quarks and antiquarks into a hadron and read off charge, strangeness, baryon number and name, with the Gell-Mann-Nishijima check.

lessons.title: The Standard Model Particle Content and the Charm Quark
objectives: List the quarks and leptons with charge and generation structure and the gauge bosons with the force each carries
Cite the evidence for colour and for a fourth and fifth quark (November Revolution, J/psi)

readings.title: The November Revolution and Its Aftermath

lectures.title: Lecture 1.1: Quantum Field and Matter (the Standard Model particle content)

demoIdeas: Standard Model table with generation, charge and force filters: click a particle to see which forces act on it and its decay channels.
Resonance scan: sweep sqrt(s) through 3.1 GeV in e+ e- collisions and see the narrow J/psi peak on top of the hadronic continuum.

lessons.title: The Yukawa Potential and the Four Forces
objectives: Derive the Yukawa potential from the massive-field equation and relate its range to the mediator mass
Compare the strengths and ranges of the four forces and the typical lifetime scale for strong, electromagnetic and weak decays
demoIdeas: Yukawa versus Coulomb: overlay potentials for different mediator masses and show the cut-off range, with the four forces' ranges and strengths on a log chart.

lessons.title: Reading and Counting Feynman Diagrams
objectives: Read a Feynman diagram as a process: identify external lines, internal lines and vertices, and track conserved charges at each vertex
Use a diagram to enumerate lowest-order contributions to a decay or scattering process
demoIdeas: Diagram builder: attach vertices according to QED rules for a chosen process, see the charge and momentum bookkeeping at each vertex and the count of lowest-order diagrams.

units.title: Relativistic Kinematics
units.summary: Four-vectors and invariants applied to particle decays, collisions, thresholds and collider energies.

lessons.title: Natural Units and Lorentz Boosts of Four-Vectors
objectives: Work in natural units (hbar = c = 1) and convert masses, lengths, lifetimes and cross sections to and from SI/MeV-fm
Apply a Lorentz boost to an energy-momentum four-vector and compute invariant mass squared
demoIdeas: Boost calculator: enter a four-vector and a boost velocity, see the transformed vector with the invariant mass held constant.
Unit converter between SI, MeV-fm and natural units for masses, lengths, lifetimes and cross sections.

lessons.title: Energy-Momentum Relations and Invariant Mass
objectives: Compute energy and momentum of a particle in the lab and centre-of-momentum frames
Use E^2 = p^2 + m^2 to decide whether a process is kinematically allowed
demoIdeas: Energy-momentum hyperbola E^2 = p^2 + m^2: slider for mass and momentum shows the allowed region, and a two-particle system's invariant mass as the opening angle changes.

lessons.title: Two-Body Decays and Chemical Analogues
objectives: Compute the final-state momenta in a two-body decay in the parent's rest frame
Apply the same algebra to a chemical analogue: kinetic-energy release in molecular fragmentation versus nuclear decay
demoIdeas: Two-body decay in the rest frame: sliders for parent and daughter masses show the fixed daughter momenta and energies, with a molecular-fragmentation preset showing the kinetic-energy sharing by mass.

lessons.title: Production Thresholds and the Collider Advantage
objectives: Compute the invariant s for fixed-target and collider setups and the threshold energy to produce a heavier state
Explain the advantage of colliders over fixed targets in available centre-of-mass energy
demoIdeas: Threshold tool: pick beam and target particles and see the minimum beam energy for a chosen final state, fixed-target versus collider.

units.title: Symmetries, Hadrons and Bound States
units.summary: Conservation laws and symmetry groups, isospin and flavour SU(3), the discrete symmetries C, P, T, and the bound-state spectroscopy of positronium, quarkonium and hadrons.

lessons.title: Noether's Theorem and the Addition of Angular Momenta
objectives: State Noether's theorem informally: each continuous symmetry gives a conserved quantity
Add two angular momenta and state the allowed total J values and the Clebsch-Gordan structure for two spin-1/2 particles
demoIdeas: Clebsch-Gordan coupler: pick j1 and j2 and see the coupled basis and coefficients as a table, with the allowed J values and multiplicities.
Vector-model picture: two angular momentum vectors precessing about the total J, with sliders for the quantum numbers.

lessons.title: Spin Singlet and Triplet States and the Chemistry Link
objectives: Construct the spin singlet and triplet states and identify their symmetry under exchange
Relate this to chemistry: electron-spin coupling in molecules, NMR J-coupling and term symbols use the same algebra
demoIdeas: Two-spin states: show the singlet and three triplet combinations as arrows, with their exchange symmetry and the energy splitting from a spin-spin coupling.

lessons.title: Isospin as a Symmetry of the Strong Interaction
objectives: Explain isospin as an SU(2) symmetry of the strong force and assign I and I3 to the nucleon, pion and delta
Combine two isospins to predict relative rates of strong reactions (e.g. pion-nucleon scattering) with Clebsch-Gordan coefficients
demoIdeas: Isospin coupler for pi N scattering: pick the charge state and see the decomposition into I = 3/2 and 1/2 channels and the resulting relative cross sections near the Delta resonance.

lessons.title: SU(3) Flavour Multiplets and Symmetry Breaking
objectives: Draw the SU(3) flavour octet and decuplet for the lowest baryons and mesons in the I3-Y plane
Explain why SU(3) flavour is only approximate and relate the mass splittings to the strange-quark mass
demoIdeas: Weight diagram: draw the SU(3) octet and decuplet in I3-Y space and click a state to see its quark content, with a slider turning on the strange-quark mass to show the mass splittings.

lessons.title: Parity and Charge Conjugation of Hadrons
objectives: Define the parity and charge-conjugation operations and assign intrinsic parity to particles and antiparticles
Compute the parity and C of a quark-antiquark meson with given L and S
demoIdeas: Meson quantum-number calculator: set L and S for a q-qbar state and read off J, P and C, flagging the allowed J^PC combinations.

lessons.title: P, C and CP Violation and the CPT Theorem
objectives: State which interactions violate P, C and CP and cite the experimental evidence (Wu experiment, neutral kaons)
State the CPT theorem and explain why it is believed to hold
demoIdeas: Mirror test: a decay-distribution viewer that flips the helicity of the decay products to show parity violation in weak versus conservation in EM decays.

lessons.title: Hydrogen-Like Atoms, Positronium and Hyperfine Structure
objectives: Scale hydrogen energy levels to positronium and to quarkonium by replacing the reduced mass and the effective coupling
Explain the hyperfine splitting of hydrogen and positronium in terms of spin-spin coupling and extend it to meson and baryon mass splittings
Relate to chemistry: reduced-mass scaling, the 21 cm line and electron-nuclear hyperfine coupling in EPR

lectures.source: MIT OCW 8.421 Atomic and Optical Physics I (Ketterle, Spring 2014)
lectures.title: Lecture 8: Atoms IV

lectures.source: MIT OCW 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Zwiebach, Fall 2013)
lectures.title: Lecture 25: Addition of Angular Momentum (cont.)

demoIdeas: Spectrum scaler: choose hydrogen, positronium or muonic hydrogen and compare level diagrams with the reduced mass and the Bohr radius labelled.

lessons.title: Quarkonium, Confinement and Baryon Magnetic Moments
objectives: Use the charmonium and bottomonium spectra as evidence for a confining potential with a Coulomb-like short-range part
Compute baryon magnetic moments in the quark model and compare with data

lectures.source: NPTEL Nuclear and Particle Physics (Poulose, IIT Guwahati)
lectures.title: Mod-07 Lec-20: Quark Model - II

demoIdeas: Spectrum scaler: charmonium and bottomonium levels in the Coulomb-plus-linear potential, with sliders for alpha_s and the string tension k.
Pulling a quark-antiquark pair apart: the flux-tube energy grows linearly until it is enough to create a new pair and the string breaks.

units.title: The Feynman Calculus
units.summary: Decay rates and cross sections from Fermi's golden rule, and the Feynman rules for a toy theory as a template for the real ones.

lessons.title: Widths, Lifetimes, Cross Sections and Luminosity
objectives: Define decay width, branching ratio, lifetime, cross section and luminosity and relate them
Relate the width to the energy uncertainty and a resonance line shape (Breit-Wigner), connecting to natural linewidth in spectroscopy
demoIdeas: Breit-Wigner: slide mass and width and see the resonance line shape, with the decay time and full width at half maximum on a parallel panel.
Collider event-rate calculator: sliders for luminosity and cross section show events per day and the integrated luminosity needed for a discovery.

lessons.title: Fermi's Golden Rule and the Two-Body Decay Rate
objectives: State Fermi's golden rule for decays and scattering with relativistic phase space and the invariant amplitude M
Derive the two-body decay rate formula in the parent rest frame
demoIdeas: Two-body phase space: sliders for the parent and daughter masses show p* and the relative decay rate, with the rate vanishing at threshold.

lessons.title: The Toy Theory: Feynman Rules and a Decay Rate
objectives: State the toy-theory Feynman rules (vertex factor, propagator, momentum conservation, integration over loop momenta)
Compute the lowest-order amplitude and decay rate for A -> B + C in the toy theory

readings.title: Feynman Rules for a Toy Theory

demoIdeas: Diagram builder: attach vertices according to toy-theory rules and see the amplitude expression assembled symbolically, then plug in masses and coupling to get the decay rate and lifetime.

lessons.title: Scattering by Virtual Exchange and the Problem of Divergences
objectives: Compute the lowest-order scattering amplitude and cross section for two particles exchanging a virtual particle
Explain why higher-order diagrams bring loop integrals that diverge and what renormalisation conceptually does about it
demoIdeas: Exchange potential: slider for mediator mass shows the t-channel propagator versus momentum transfer and the resulting amplitude, approaching a contact interaction at low q.
Loop-momentum cutoff slider showing how a one-loop integral grows with the cutoff and how absorbing it into a renormalised coupling gives a finite answer.

units.title: Quantum Electrodynamics and Chromodynamics
units.summary: The Dirac equation and Feynman rules for QED, standard QED processes, running coupling, and the colour theory of quarks with confinement and asymptotic freedom.

lessons.title: The Dirac Equation, Spinors and Antiparticles
objectives: Write the Dirac equation and the gamma-matrix algebra, and solve for free-particle spinors of spin up and down
Explain how negative-energy solutions are reinterpreted as antiparticles
demoIdeas: Dirac spinor viewer: plot the four-component spinor for chosen momentum and spin and see the small-component growth with velocity.
Dirac sea picture: remove a negative-energy electron to create a hole and see it behave as a positron.

lessons.title: QED Feynman Rules and Tree-Level Amplitudes
objectives: State the polarisation vectors of the photon and the QED vertex and propagator factors
Assemble the amplitude for a tree-level QED process (e.g. electron-muon scattering) from the rules

readings.title: The Feynman Rules for Quantum Electrodynamics

demoIdeas: Process assembler for e- mu- -> e- mu-: click vertices and propagators to build the amplitude, with a slider for the scattering angle showing the photon virtuality q^2.

lessons.title: Casimir's Trick and Tree-Level QED Cross Sections
objectives: Use Casimir's trick to convert a spin-averaged squared amplitude into a trace of gamma matrices
Compute the lowest-order cross section for electron-muon scattering or electron-positron annihilation to muon pairs
demoIdeas: Differential cross section for e+ e- -> mu+ mu- versus angle with a beam-energy slider, showing the 1 + cos^2 theta angular distribution and the total 4 pi alpha^2 / 3s.

lessons.title: Vacuum Polarisation, the Running Coupling and Loop Corrections
objectives: Explain vacuum polarisation as charge screening and state how alpha runs with energy
Relate the Lamb shift and the anomalous magnetic moment of the electron to loop corrections (spectroscopy connection)

lectures.title: Lecture 4.9: Renormalization and Higher-Order QED Diagrams

demoIdeas: Running coupling: plot alpha(Q) and alpha_s(Q) against energy and mark the Z mass, with a slider for the number of active fermion flavours.

lessons.title: Colour, the R Ratio and the Feynman Rules of QCD
objectives: Explain the role of colour in baryon wave functions (Delta++) and in the ratio R = sigma(hadrons)/sigma(mu mu)
State the Feynman rules of QCD, including the three- and four-gluon vertices, and the colour factor 4/3
demoIdeas: R-ratio plot: step-function pattern of R versus sqrt(s) across quark thresholds with resonances, with a toggle for N_c = 1 versus 3.
Colour-flow explorer: pick a QCD vertex and see the colour lines and the colour factor 4/3.

lessons.title: Asymptotic Freedom, Jets and Confinement
objectives: Explain how gluon self-interaction produces antiscreening and asymptotic freedom, contrasted with QED screening
Describe deep inelastic scattering and the parton picture, jets at colliders, and confinement/hadronisation
demoIdeas: alpha_s(Q) running with sliders for Lambda and n_f, and a toggle for QED-like screening versus gluon antiscreening.
Jet formation: pull a quark-antiquark pair apart and watch string breaking produce a jet of hadrons.

units.title: Weak Interactions and Neutrinos
units.summary: Charged-current weak decays, the V-A structure, quark mixing, and neutrino masses and oscillations.

lessons.title: Charged Weak Decays and the V-A Structure
objectives: Draw and interpret the lowest-order diagrams for muon decay, neutron beta decay and charged-pion decay
Explain the V-A structure, left-handed projection and helicity suppression of pion decay to electrons relative to muons
demoIdeas: Pion decay helicity viewer: toggle between pi -> mu nu and pi -> e nu and see the spin and momentum arrows required by V-A, explaining the helicity suppression.

lessons.title: Decay-Rate Scaling, the CKM Matrix and CP Violation
objectives: Write the CKM matrix, state its role in flavour-changing decays, and explain the origin of CP violation as a complex phase
Estimate decay rates by dimensional analysis using the Fermi constant, including the G_F^2 m^5 scaling
demoIdeas: CKM unitarity triangle: plot the triangle for measured matrix elements and shrink the error bars.
Decay-rate scaling: slider for the lepton mass shows lifetime versus mass^5 on a log-log plot.

lessons.title: Flavour Mixing and the Two-Flavour Oscillation Formula
objectives: Explain how a mismatch between flavour and mass eigenstates produces oscillations and derive the two-flavour oscillation probability
Compute oscillation lengths for given energy and mass-squared difference and interpret solar and atmospheric experiments
demoIdeas: Oscillation lab: set theta, delta m^2, energy and baseline and watch the flavour probabilities versus L/E.

lessons.title: Neutrino Masses, the PMNS Matrix and Majorana Neutrinos
objectives: State the PMNS matrix structure and the evidence for non-zero neutrino masses
Describe the Dirac versus Majorana question and neutrinoless double beta decay

lectures.title: Lecture 8.5: Results of Neutrino Oscillation Experiments

demoIdeas: Three-flavour oscillation plot with the PMNS angles as sliders and a mass-ordering toggle (normal versus inverted), showing the flavour composition of each mass state as a bar.

units.title: Gauge Theories, Electroweak Unification and the Higgs
units.summary: Local gauge invariance as the organising principle, electroweak unification, and the Higgs mechanism, at a qualitative-to-semi-quantitative level.

lessons.title: Local Gauge Invariance and Non-Abelian Gauge Theory
objectives: Show that requiring local U(1) phase invariance of the Dirac Lagrangian forces a massless photon field to appear
Generalise to non-Abelian gauge theory (Yang-Mills) and say why gauge bosons of SU(2) and SU(3) self-interact
demoIdeas: Gauge-fix sandbox: apply a position-dependent phase to a wave function and watch the covariant derivative compensate with a gauge field.

lessons.title: Electroweak SU(2) x U(1) and the Mass Problem
objectives: State the field content of electroweak SU(2)xU(1), the weak mixing angle and the relations among W, Z and photon couplings
Explain why explicit mass terms for gauge bosons and chiral fermions break gauge invariance
demoIdeas: Weinberg-angle mixer: slider for theta_W rotates W3 and B into Z and photon, with the resulting couplings and the m_W = m_Z cos(theta_W) relation.

lessons.title: Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking and the Higgs Mechanism
objectives: Explain spontaneous symmetry breaking with the Mexican-hat potential and identify the Goldstone modes
Explain how the Higgs mechanism gives mass to W and Z and to fermions without breaking gauge invariance
demoIdeas: Mexican hat: rotate and tilt the potential to see the vacuum selection and the massive radial versus massless angular modes.

lessons.title: Higgs Phenomenology and the Open Problems
objectives: State the Higgs production and decay channels used at the LHC and the measured mass and couplings
List the open problems: hierarchy, neutrino masses, dark matter, matter-antimatter asymmetry
demoIdeas: Higgs branching-ratio chart versus mass, with a slider for m_H marking 125 GeV and the channels that dominate there.
